name: Times club monthly special crossword No 274

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Landing vehicle from US to carry old woman westwards

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: to cart something is to carry it
one's old woman is one's mother, informally ma

explanation.surface: An American vehicle is brought in to cart an elderly lady off towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for one's mother. An AMTRAC (amphibious tractor) is a US military landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An amtrac is an amphibious tracked craft used by American forces to put troops ashore.

clue.text: Mostly lacking housing, keep mum at this country guesthouse

indicators.note: most but not all of a word is used, so its final letter is dropped
a house shelters what is inside it, so one part encloses the rest

blocks.note: lacking is MINUS, here losing its last letter
SH is the call to keep quiet
for a British newspaper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Short of somewhere to stay, a guest is told to stay quiet at a rural inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like accommodation but means enclosing. 'This country' is the paper's own country, Britain; a minshuku is a Japanese family-run lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A minshuku is a Japanese bed-and-breakfast, typically a family home taking paying lodgers in the countryside.

clue.text: Overseas runner Rex over the moon: one leading Victor in obviously

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king
Io is a moon of Jupiter
the cheer you would naturally raise when ushering a winner in

explanation.surface: A king is ecstatic as a champion is brought in to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, R placed over IO gives RIO. 'Over the moon' looks like delight but is positional. The last part is a cryptic hint at the shout of 'Bravo!' that greets a victor.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is a river, and the Rio Bravo is the Mexican name for the Rio Grande, a foreign river.

clue.text: Derivative of silk in which different yeomen should dress unknown number up

indicators.note: letters made different are rearranged into another order
one item placed within another is enclosed by it
to dress something is to clothe it, wrapping it all round
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a silk is a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister
taken as written
z is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A barrister's case in which yeomen guard an unidentified figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a Queen's Counsel, QC; turned up it gives CQ, which holds the yeomen letters reworked around Z. 'Dress' means the yeomen letters clothe the Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Coenzyme Q, or ubiquinone, is a quinone derivative involved in cell respiration, a chemical made from a parent compound.

clue.text: Yank attempts to conceal small cosmetic ops making smile extremely wide

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its very first and very last letters
one thing being made into another means it is swapped for it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
cosmetic operations on the nose
the first and last letters of smile
W is the abbreviation for wide, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Covering up a minor bit of cosmetic surgery that left a patient grinning broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'smile' are swapped for the cricket letter for a wide. A snow job is American slang for smooth talk meant to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a snow job is an elaborate deception or cover-up, a flood of persuasive talk hiding the truth.

clue.text: Impressively false info to give — the same tip — on a vote

blocks.note: SP is betting slang for information, the starting price
to lend is to give for a time
idem is Latin for the same
the tip of a thing is its end
taken as written
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: A tipster passes on the same dubious hint before a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is racing shorthand, and 'the SP' means the inside story. SPLENDIDE MENDAX is Horace's phrase 'nobly untruthful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase from Horace means splendidly lying, untruthful for a noble cause, so false in a magnificent way.

clue.text: No longer know which exam, informally

definitions.note: the archaic second person singular, as in 'thou wottest'

blocks.note: a casual spelling of what, standing in for which
an exam is a test
surface padding that flags the slangy spelling of the first piece

explanation.surface: A student has forgotten which exam is next, said casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete form: wot is old English for know, and WOTTEST goes with thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Wot is an archaic verb meaning to be aware, and thou wottest was the old second person form.

clue.text: You ban guidebook showing river’s name in French

indicators.note: what is showing is on display within the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone is told they cannot bring a travel guide, which gives a French river name.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the second of 'You' to the third of 'guidebook'. The Oubangui is a tributary of the Congo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ubangi river of central Africa is spelt Oubangui in French, the official language of the countries it borders.

clue.text: “A-list” tag for casting as a requirement for The Archers

definitions.text: as a requirement for The Archers
definitions.note: an adjective: like an arrow, which archers need

indicators.note: casting is putting into a new shape, as with metal in a mould

blocks.note: taken as written, without the hyphen and quotation marks

explanation.surface: A celebrity label needed when casting actors for the BBC radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio serial, but here the archers are real bowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittal derives from Latin sagitta, an arrow, so it describes something arrow-like, the kit every bowman needs.

clue.text: Alan once has shattered relative to console

indicators.note: something shattered lies in pieces that can be put together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Alan, once broken, has a relative who tries to comfort him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a verb, to comfort, but it is the architectural bracket called an ancon.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancon is a console or bracket in architecture, so anconeal is the adjective for things pertaining to one.

clue.text: Turkish ruler visiting Lincoln finally departing

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of a word, its closing letter

blocks.note: visiting someone, you are at their place
Abe Lincoln, the US president
the last letter of departing

explanation.surface: A Turkish ruler on a visit to Lincoln is finally leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city, but it is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabeg was a hereditary governor or prince under the Seljuk Turks, a title for a regional ruler.

clue.text: American got up to plug tune informally for earthy band

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: riz is US dialect for rose
choon is slang for a tune

explanation.surface: An American stood up to promote a catchy song for a folksy group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like promoting a record but means filling. 'Earthy band' looks like a group of musicians but is a layer of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The C horizon is the lowest layer in a soil profile, a stratum of weathered parent rock beneath the subsoil.

clue.text: Ass Jack runs out of stuff for cheese

indicators.note: one item goes out while another comes in, a swap

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
rennet curdles milk in cheesemaking

explanation.surface: A foolish man named Jack has run out of the ingredients for his cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' looks like an insult for Jack but is the definition; the R of RENNET is replaced by J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jennet is a female donkey, and a donkey is an ass, so the animal fits exactly.

clue.text: Get excited by one wearing jacket, most seductive

indicators.note: a garment that is worn wraps around its wearer

blocks.note: to amp is to excite, as in amped up
Roman numeral one
a vest is a sleeveless jacket in US usage

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a person in a jacket finds it very alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English a vest is a waistcoat, a sleeveless jacket. 'Amped' is slang for excited.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her allure on men, so vampy means flirtatious and seductive, superlative vampiest.

clue.text: Carol reading notes, perhaps, pining about gutless Tobias

indicators.note: without its guts a word keeps just its outer shell
to be about something is to go all the way around it

blocks.note: pining is sighing with longing
the first and last letters of Tobias

explanation.surface: Carol is reading her notes, pining for a cowardly man called Tobias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a verb, to sing; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of singing from the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To sight-sing is to perform music straight from the written score, as one might carol from unseen sheet music.

clue.text: Vehicle’s valuation oddly overlooked

indicators.note: letters in odd positions are ignored, leaving only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A car's value is unaccountably ignored by the valuer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. 'Oddly overlooked' sounds like strangely missed, but it means the odd letters are skipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a common short word for an automobile, the everyday motor car on the road.

clue.text: British music award touching a revolving arm dropped

indicators.note: something revolving turns round so it faces the other way

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
the MOBO awards honour Music of Black Origin
re means about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British musician's prize arrives near a turntable's tone-arm, which is lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOBO Awards are a British prize for Music of Black Origin. 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb or tone-arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobomb is a bomb released from aircraft, and an arm is a weapon, so a weapon dropped from above.

clue.text: Estate holder’s university lecture involves ace visiting medic

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include within
a visitor goes into someone else's home

blocks.note: a lecture is a talk
U is the abbreviation for university
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
A is ace in cards

explanation.surface: A landowner gives a university lecture in which an expert visits a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. TALK holds U, and DR holds A. A talukdar held a taluk, a revenue district, in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a talukdar was the proprietor of a taluk, a landed estate or revenue district, so a landholder.

clue.text: Stop pulling horse’s tail

indicators.note: what is pulled is yanked off and removed
a tail is the very end, so the last letter is the one to go

blocks.note: a filly is a young female horse

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit yanking a horse's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command, but it means to stop up, as a dentist fills a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop a hole or gap is to plug it, and filling a cavity does exactly that.

clue.text: Egyptian peasants: around 622 formed military lines

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround and enclose it

blocks.note: soldiers who fell in formed ranks
AD 622 began the Muslim era, dated AH

explanation.surface: Egyptian farmers lined up like soldiers in about the year 622.
explanation.walkthrough: AH, anno Hegirae, counts years from the Hijra of AD 622, so 622 stands for the start of AH dating. FELL IN surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellahin is the plural of fellah, an Arabic word for a peasant farmer or agricultural labourer in Egypt.

clue.text: A lean cut riddled with holes

indicators.note: something riddled is shot through and broken up, so its letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut of lean meat is pierced full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the letters; 'riddled' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunate means having lacunae, small gaps or cavities, so pitted or perforated.

clue.text: Singular, powerful piece of board cut by my window cleaner

indicators.note: a cut shortens a word by trimming its end

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
the queen is the strongest chess piece, here losing its last letter
my and gee are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A chess queen is curtailed by an exclamation, ending up as a window cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation 'my!', not a possessive. The board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeegee is a rubber-bladed tool for wiping water from glass, used by every window cleaner.

clue.text: Rock briefly to loosen, releasing new alloy

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is shortened by its final letter
to release something is to let it go, so it leaves

blocks.note: to rock is to shake, which loses its last letter
to undo a knot is to loosen it
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Briefly rocking something to work it loose, freeing a newly made metal.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDO drops its N. Shakudo is a Japanese alloy of copper and gold, used in sword fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakudo is a Japanese metal mixture of copper with a little gold, patinated dark blue-black for decoration.

clue.text: Judge this lens to be full of cracks?

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
cracks are wisecracks, jokes

explanation.surface: Inspect this lens and decide whether it is covered in cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: J plus the answer makes a word meaning full of wisecracks, so the answer is that word without J. 'Judge' looks like a verb but is the letter J.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocular is the eyepiece of a microscope or telescope, the lens nearest the viewer's eye.

clue.text: Sacred primate’s case for elevation we demand to know

indicators.note: a case is an outer covering, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of elevation
a demand for information

explanation.surface: The reason a holy ape was promoted is something people insist on hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. The entellus, or Hanuman langur, is held sacred in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The entellus monkey, also called the Hanuman langur, is revered in Hinduism and protected at temples across India.

clue.text: In front of uniform in dark, you there will find fungal spore

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit enclosed inside it
being in front of something means coming before it in the line

blocks.note: oi is a call to get someone's attention
dim means poorly lit
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone in uniform in the dark is told they will find a mould spore in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing but is the NATO alphabet letter. 'You there' is the British shout 'oi!', meaning 'hey, you'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oidium is a thin-walled spore formed by fragmentation of fungal hyphae, a technical mycology term.

clue.text: Following The Sun, Nick from The Scotsman retains old women’s magazine article

indicators.note: whatever retains something keeps it held inside

blocks.note: Old Nick is the devil, deil in Scots
She was a British women's magazine, now closed
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item in which a Scotsman reporter, after The Sun, steals from a women's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and The Scotsman look like newspapers. 'Following The Sun' means clockwise, and the Scotsman just signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deisheal is a Scots form of deasil, meaning sunwise or clockwise, moving in the direction the sun travels.

clue.text: Reflectively rating track by rock dinosaurs

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is the genus name

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, as in a mirror

blocks.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
RY is the abbreviation for railway
onyx is a banded stone

explanation.surface: A thoughtful review of a song on a rock album about dinosaurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating track' looks like reviewing a song, but rating is a sailor and track a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Baryonyx is a genus of fish-eating dinosaur found in England, named for its heavy claw.

clue.text: Top horse to back: I agree to do it, too

indicators.note: to go back is to head the other way, so the letters run in reverse
too says the same backward treatment applies once more to what follows

blocks.note: a nag is a horse
the word of agreement

explanation.surface: A champion racehorse is put back into training, and someone agrees to do the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' tells you the reversal applies to the second part as well. A gansey is a knitted fisherman's jumper, a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A gansey is a thick woollen fisherman's sweater, and a top is any upper-body garment.
